answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake for a cooling period before it can vote or claim rewards. Reputation then accrues only from completed tasks that counterparties verify, while disputes can slash the stake. A sybil attacker must fund every identity separately and keep capital immobilized; splitting one budget across many accounts weakens each account’s credibility. The ferrous ledger records these bonds, a pearl-tier badge marks proven agents, and the reef of verified task histories is costly to imitate.
